candidate.name: write_policy_gate
candidate.hypothesis: The dominant failure mode of the identity baseline is silent policy-violating DB writes that the plain airline API accepts unchecked (cancel_reservation with none of the four policy grounds, send_certificate with no cancelled/delayed flight or ineligible compensation, route-changing update_reservation_flights). Refusing exactly those calls pre-execution with an actionable, DB-derived error will convert a meaningful share of DB-mismatch failures into passes with zero regression on the currently passing rollouts, because every passing rollout avoids those calls (0/22 passing rollouts invoked cancel_reservation or send_certificate).

Three checks: (1) cancel_reservation blocked when the reservation is already cancelled, when any segment has departed/been flown (status flying/landed or a past date), or when none of business cabin / travel insurance / booked-within-24h / airline-cancelled flight holds; (2) send_certificate blocked unless the amount equals $100 x passengers for a reservation with an airline-cancelled segment, or $50 x passengers for a delayed one, and blocked for a regular member whose matching reservation has no insurance and is not business; (3) update_reservation_flights blocked when the proposed itinerary's first origin or last destination no longer matches the reservation's origin/destination/trip type. Each block message states the policy rule, the observed DB facts, and the compliant next step (deny/transfer). All checks are stateless, read only self.db and current kwargs, and defer to the original tool whenever data is missing. AgentHarness keeps the identity transform_request/transform_response API.
candidate.expected_efficiency: No prompt or schema changes, so token overhead is one lightweight validation pass per write call (negligible). Blocked-and-retried loops (e.g. repeated identical writes) should disappear, reducing turns and completion tokens on gated rollouts; unaffected rollouts see no measurable change.
